NEGATIVO sense(b): headline result IS that dedicated memory systems underperform naive full-context ICL -- systematic negative evidence about current memory-management mechanisms. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (gain metric), FIDELIDAD (concept-drift/staleness design), COSTO (explicit $/rollout table).

title: Manufactured Confidence: How Memory Consolidation Turns Hearsay into Confident Facts
benchmarks: own constructed diagnostic harness (running-total computation + budget-approval agent + access-control agent); tested against mem0, LangMem, and a verbatim VectorStoreRetrieverMemory control
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Manufactured confidence': fact-extraction consolidation (mem0, LangMem) rewrites a casual, hedged remark into a confident, dated assertion that later agent steps obey like a verified fact. TWO sources: (1) natural staleness -- a once-true hedge goes stale and its correction is never stored (no attacker needed), producing confident-wrong grants on 0.69 (mem0)/0.75 (LangMem) of requests (Table3); (2) adversarial injection -- one planted sentence is laundered into an authoritative dated fact by BOTH real products (100% laundering rate) vs 0% on the verbatim control (Table7), yielding 0.72 unauthorized-grant with no defense (Table6). 'The obvious fixes fail': a passive 'unverified' tag is leaky and provider-dependent (0.00-0.81, Table5/6); an active 'do not trust this' instruction (distrust) stops the cascade everywhere (0.00 wrong-decision) but by ABDICATION not discrimination -- it escalates 100% of requests even on CORRECT memory (Table8). The fix that actually works: preserve tentative phrasing AT THE STORE (do not de-hedge; hygiene, not an adversarial defense) PLUS add a redundant/second source (authoritative directory) to verify against, which restores correct discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00, zero escalation, Table2) even under an assertive poisoned memory.
cita: Kwon (2026). Manufactured Confidence: How Memory Consolidation Turns Hearsay into Confident Facts.
notes: S1/Fig1: memory products (mem0, LangMem) extract conversation into stored 'facts' retrieved by later steps -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (extracted text facts), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS (paper explicitly probes the underlying BGE-small vector: hedge IS linearly recoverable there, balanced accuracy 1.00, so the loss happens at the LLM-rewrite/consolidation step, not the embedding -- CONSOLIDACION is the operation under study, title-level). S3 cross of 7 framings (bare/attributed/forged-authority all confident vs 4 hedge types) isolates that the agent obeys CONFIDENCE not SOURCE (Table1: confident framings grant 0.81 regardless of attribution/forged 'system of record'; hedges collapse grants near 0.00). Table3: with an in-context correction present, memory reconciles/downgrades (ACTUALIZACION, grants 0/16); without one, staleness persists (grants 0.69-0.75) -- direct fidelidad_procedencia=SI evidence (this IS the paper's core axis: staleness + provenance-blindness). Table2: redundant authoritative-directory source restores discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00). 5 models tested (Claude Sonnet/Haiku, Llama-70B, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen-72B), all deterministic at temp=0 -- systematic controlled manipulation of framing/defense/source = ABLATION per calibration vara E (not a standard task BENCHMARK-E2E). handoff=CONTENIDO: 'LLM agents carry conclusions across steps AND SESSIONS in compressed memory' -- the manufactured-confident fact IS the content that travels. NEGATIVO sense(b) + SEGURIDAD (cs.CR; explicit memory-poisoning/injection attack, 'PoisonedRAG corrupts what is retrieved; we study a memory-store variant that corrupts what is recorded'). F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, SEGURIDAD, WRITE.

title: ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education
benchmarks: own paper-section Manim-animation dataset (memory-building 39 tasks / fixed-probe 33 / cross-test 40); baselines: Manim-code RAG, Random EMB, VLM-reflection-only
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Cross-task forgetting' (S1, Fig.1): a reflection pipeline closes the INTRA-task loop (observe error, revise, retry) but every lesson paid for in tokens is thrown away before the next task starts, so a structurally similar future task repeats the same layout/formula mistake and pays the full reflection cost again. Mitigated by the dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank: positive channel M+ = soft Reference Examples (success rationale, write-gated at score>=85), negative channel M- = hard Known Pitfalls (validated failure->success transitions, causal-attribution gated, requires score delta>=5 for visual transitions) injected into the Coder prompt on retrieval. Table1/Fig3: EMB@200 improves blind-human Pass@1 to 84.9% (vs 68.5% VLM-reflection-only, 69.6% Random-EMB, and even 83.3% for a strong matched-budget static Manim-code RAG baseline) while cutting reflection rounds to 6.5 (vs 12.2 baseline).
cita: Jiang et al. (2026). ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education.
notes: S3.1-3.3: dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank M=M+ union M-, backed by 1 SQLite table + 2 per-polarity Faiss IndexFlatIP vector indices (representacion=HIBRIDA); M+ records a success rationale (soft prior, PROCEDIMENTAL template) per high-scoring scene (u*>=theta_high=85, ADMISION); M- records a structured 'validated failure pattern' (EPISODICA, causal-attribution-gated: crash->success text transitions accepted unconditionally, visual transitions require delta_fail>=5 score-margin, ADMISION) via LLM-distilled lessons (NOT literal diffs -- explicit CONSOLIDACION step). Retrieval by task-embedding cosine similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, EMBEDDINGS), disjoint per-polarity indices (a query on M+ never returns M- records). Explicit six named agents (Storyboarder, Coder, text Reviewer, VLM Reviewer, Visual Reviser, Lesson Distiller/Rationale Writer) sharing the single EMB -> multiagente=SI (paper self-describes as 'self-evolving multi-agent system'). S3.3 'Provenance, deduplication, and embedder pinning': provenance block (run id, scene id, extraction source, transition ordinal, before/after scores) for write-time dedup; embedder identity PINNED at first creation, 'refused on reopen if a different encoder is requested' preventing silent re-embedding drift between writes/reads -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. 'No capacity, no eviction... grow monotonically' -- explicitly NO OLVIDO mechanism. Table1 ablations (channel isolation No-M+/No-M-/No-memory, gate stringency, Top-1 retrieval depth, Weak-VLM reviewer) directly measure read-side utility -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): M- is explicitly a negative/failure channel storing 'Known Pitfalls' (validated failures) as first-class memory content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION (LLM-distilled lessons), FIDELIDAD (provenance/embedder-pinning), MULTIAGENTE, WRITE.

title: MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation
benchmarks: LongMemEval-S (500 questions, 50+ sessions/user, 3 model families); strategies compared: S0-no-memory, S_rand-random-RAG, S1-full-context, S4-RAG-MiniLM, S4b-RAG-cloud-embedding, S2-agent-scratchpad self-memory, S3-Mem0
fallos_mitigaciones: Agent self-memory (scratchpad) failure: the 4,096-token scratchpad 'collapses on multi-session questions (3.3%), where it cannot retain enough detail across 50+ sessions' -- 'compression is a wager: each write decides what future questions will not need' (S4.1); self-memory (42%) underperforms basic retrieval (47%). No mitigation for this is implemented; the paper's own contribution is methodological, not architectural: fix the embedding model across comparisons, stratify by model family, and report write-path cost before attributing gains to memory architecture (S1/S6).
cita: Wang (2026). MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation.
notes: Pure measurement/methodology paper (Table1: 7 strategies S0/Srand/S1/S4/S4b/S2/S3, no own memory architecture) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S3 protocol: 6 controlled pairwise comparisons each varying EXACTLY one factor (Table2): S4 vs S4b isolates embedding choice ONLY (+6.2pp, p=0.004, identical code/chunking/top-k/model/judge) -> this IS a direct retrieval-quality measurement -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Headline finding (S4.1, matches abstract): Mem0 beats MiniLM-RAG by +11pp but LOSES to cloud-embedding RAG by -1.2pp -- 'one variable flips the conclusion' (Fig1 case study) -> NEGATIVO sense(b), core architectural-memory-gain claims are often embedding confounds not real memory-method wins. S4.2: same S1-vs-S4 comparison gives 3 DIFFERENT conclusions across GPT-4o-mini/Sonnet/Gemini (Sonnet refuses 63% of full-context queries) -> model-behavior confound. S4.5 knowledge-update question type requires 'identify which of several conflicting facts is the most recent' -- a direct staleness-resolution axis where full-context (72%) beats retrieval (62-63%) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Table6/7: write-path cost audited as first-class metric (S0 $0/0s -> S4b $0.01/60s -> S2 $0.34/90min/~250 LLM calls -> S3(Mem0) $0.50+/120min/1000+ calls) -> COSTO-TOKENS+LATENCIA; on 88 matched instances Mem0(72.7%) does NOT beat cloud-RAG(73.9%, p=1.0) at 50x the cost. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, COSTO.

title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
benchmarks: MemSyco-Bench (own, 5 task categories); systems evaluated: No-Memory, Full-Dialog, NaiveRAG, Mem0, A-Mem, LightMem, MemGPT, MemoryBank, SuperMemory (2 backbones: Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Memory-induced sycophancy' (S3.1): retrieved historical user beliefs/preferences/statements can be outdated, out-of-scope, or contradicted by objective evidence, yet the agent treats them as evidentiary signal and shifts its answer toward the remembered claim instead of following current evidence -- distinct from ordinary sycophancy because the source is retrieved MEMORY (possibly absent from the current query), the failure extends to scope-violation/evidence-override (not just agreement), and it persists/repeats across sessions. No mitigation is proposed by this benchmark (diagnostic only): S2.1 preliminary study shows adding a memory snippet drops factual accuracy (largest drop DeepSeek-V4-Flash 56.1%->40.2%) while sycophancy rate rises (24.3%->52.3%); Table1 main results show EVERY evaluated memory system (Mem0/A-Mem/LightMem/MemGPT/MemoryBank/SuperMemory) INCREASES sycophancy rate on Objective-Fact-Judgment relative to a No-Memory floor and DECREASES accuracy relative to No-Memory on both backbones.
cita: Xiang et al. (2026). MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory.
notes: Pure diagnostic benchmark (no own memory mechanism, evaluates 8 systems + No-Memory/Full-Dialog controls) -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S1/S3.2: explicit design intent 'shifting the evaluation focus from RETRIEVAL SUCCESS to POST-RETRIEVAL memory use' -- S2.2 preliminary error-cause analysis on LongMemEval/LoCoMo/STALE/PersonaMem shows their errors are 47.4-66.1% retrieval-failure(R-/A-) vs only 5.8-13.7% post-retrieval-failure(R+/A-), motivating this benchmark's post-retrieval focus -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (measures what happens AFTER successful retrieval). 5 task categories (S3.2): Objective-Fact-Judgment, Contextual-Scope-Control, Memory-Evidence-Conflict (suppress inapplicable memory); Valid-Memory-Selection ('identify the currently valid preference when a user's preference has been updated, reversed, or replaced' -- direct staleness-tracking), Personalized-Memory-Use (valid personalization) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (Valid-Memory-Selection is exactly a staleness/update-tracking axis). Metrics (S3.4): Generation Accuracy (all tasks) + Sycophancy Rate (first 3 tasks) + Memory-Use Metrics (Correct-Mem-Use / Outdated-Mem for last 2 tasks) -> bespoke OTRA metrics alongside EXITO. Table1 (Qwen3-8B): Objective-Fact-Judgment Sycophancy Rate jumps from an effective ~0.67(no-memory floor) to 69-99% with ANY memory system present; accuracy drops from 49.12%(No-Memory) to 26-36% across all 7 memory conditions -- systematic degradation from adding memory. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (post-retrieval-use focus).

title: When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces
benchmarks: GovMem-Bench (own controlled synthetic); project-internal real-trace subset (120 human-gold candidates / 79 recorded traces + project reports); external SWE-agent/OpenHands trajectory stress tests (2x50-trajectory pilots + a 361-candidate V2 pool + a 133-row human-adjudicated high-impact packet)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'False promotion from correlated agent traces': repeated observations across agents are NOT necessarily independent evidence -- the same claim may be copied from a shared source, induced by a shared prompt/tool, stale under a new environment, adversarial, or valid only in a narrower scope (S1). Naive promotion turns 'long-term memory into a persistence layer for correlated errors.' Mitigated by GovMem: (1) dependency-aware support estimation (groups observations by dependency structure -- copied/shared-prompt/shared-tool observations do NOT count as independent votes), (2) counterevidence retrieval + scope-compatibility check, (3) promote/reject/needs-review triage. Controlled GovMem-Bench: reduces false promotion 0.597(raw)->0.040 preserving 0.960 recall. Project-internal real traces: reduces false promotion 0.371(source+scope)->0.032 but held-out FP remains 0.111, recall drops to 0.448, review burden 0.692 -- i.e. the safety gain is largely reviewer-routing, not automatic promotion. CRITICALLY, final human adjudication of a 133-row high-impact external packet found ZERO safe automatic promotions and REJECTED ALL 11 of GovMem's own local verification-gate positives (mistaken pytest boilerplate/file-dumps/non-reusable-debugging-traces for verified evidence) -- so even GovMem's own output does not survive independent human review, a genuinely negative finding about the method's own limits, not just naive baselines.
cita: Qi et al. (2026). When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces.
notes: S3 GovMem = a conservative write-path AUDITOR side-agent, task-independent from the agents that write traces: task agents emit traces -> a memory proposer normalizes candidate memories (aggregated similar observations + provenance metadata: source, prompt family, parent event, environment, trust) -> GovMem's 4-step audit (form candidate -> estimate dependency-aware support via a PROVENANCE/DEPENDENCY GRAPH among observations, NOT sample-similarity -> retrieve+classify counterevidence & check scope -> output promote/reject/needs-review) BEFORE the write reaches long-term storage -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION (this IS the paper's central operation), retrieval=GRAFO (dependency lineage graph traversal for counterevidence), mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL(reusable lessons)+EPISODICA(trace-derived observations), consistent with related-work framing (ExpeL/LEGOMem-style reusable memories). Index Terms explicitly list 'multi-agent systems' + repeated-multi-agent-observation framing throughout ('Multi-agent traces: A observes X, B repeats X, C: stale X', Fig1) -> multiagente=SI. Table III (GovMem-Bench, controlled synthetic mechanism experiments: true-independent/true-copied/false-copied/false-correlated/stale/adversarial/out-of-scope candidate types) is the ABLATION evidence; Table IV/VIII (real-trace + 133-row external human-adjudication) is BENCHMARK-E2E. GovMem-verified is NOT strictly dominant: 'review-all-correlated' baseline nearly matches its internal false-promotion (0.033 vs 0.032) with HIGHER recall (0.881 vs 0.448) and LOWER review burden (0.492 vs 0.692) -- 'GovMem should be read as one point in a risk-control design space,' explicitly NOT claiming universal dominance. NEGATIVO sense(b): the paper's OWN headline external result is that surface verification and repeated trace evidence are insufficient for safe automatic promotion, even under the proposed governance mechanism. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds MULTIAGENTE, SEGURIDAD (adversarial candidate type tested; evidence-governance/provenance framing explicitly parallels memory-poisoning defense literature, cites A-MemGuard).

title: Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory
benchmarks: own pre-registered gate suite M0-M4: synthetic-facts recall (M0/M1), consolidation stress test (M2), brain-vs-RAG controlled comparison (M3), hidden-rule-discovery agentic task (M4, 60 episodes)
fallos_mitigaciones: TWO mechanisms explicitly KILLED by pre-registered gates, not salvaged: (1) Repetition-weighted ranking VIOLATES cue-specificity -- 'a distractor at sim=0.87 with strength 4 outranks the correct singleton at 0.95' (10/10 first failures inspected); loses to vanilla cosine RAG by -0.440 (multiplicative scoring) and -0.180 (cue-gated tie-breaking, delta=0.07 band); 'as pre-declared, strength ranking was removed from the default system' -- no fix attempted, the mechanism was simply killed. (2) Cosine-only deduplication is 'structurally unsound': validated same-fact paraphrase similarities (median 0.83) completely overlap same-template-distractor similarities (median 0.87) -- 'no threshold exists.' Mitigated by adding an LLM same-fact judge (12/12 on a probe set) instead of relying on embedding threshold alone, and by BANNING LLM-paraphrase summarization during consolidation (observed 'inventing field contents' / corrupting exact values) in favor of verbatim-text retention -- 'verbatim beats gist, twice' (both M2 consolidation and M4 lesson-writing).
cita: Raviotta (2026). Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory.
notes: S3: memory = SQLite graph over a plain-text vault; nodes are episodic/semantic memories (mem_tipos) with embedding+strength-counter+archived-flag; edges reinforced on co-recall, decay over time, dropped below threshold (OLVIDO) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (graph+embeddings). Same-fact judge gates writes (ADMISION); re-exposures bump strength / create edge instead of duplicate (ACTUALIZACION); nightly selective-consolidation cycle fuses re-exposure-connected clusters into ONE semantic node keeping verbatim text of the strongest member (CONSOLIDACION, explicit CHECKPOINT trigger); episodics archived not deleted. 5 pre-registered falsifiable gates (floor=no-memory arm, ceiling=oracle arm, bootstrap 95% CIs, PASS/PARTIAL/KILL fixed BEFORE runs) -- M0 establishes recall utility (naked 0.00 -> memory 0.98), M1 finds a repetition-learning-curve LATER shown (M3) to be self-inflicted interference -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is the paper's entire methodological core. M4 (main result, matches abstract): frozen 9B agent + memory converts verbatim API-error lessons into procedural competence, first-try success 0.45->1.00 over 2 blocks of 20 unseen episodes vs memoryless control flat at 0.00 for all 60, oracle 0.95; seed replication 3/3 on the categorical transfer effect (memory>>control), 1/3 on within-run curve significance at n=20/block -- reported HONESTLY as PARTIAL where applicable. NEGATIVO BOTH senses: (a) 'we report everything: two clean passes, two kills of mechanisms we had previously celebrated' (explicit negative-results publication, rare in the field per abstract); (b) systematic negative evidence that popular mechanisms (strength-weighted ranking, embedding-only dedup) actively HURT vs a trivial baseline. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;NEGATIVO) + adds FIDELIDAD (verbatim-vs-gist corruption findings), PROCEDIMENTAL, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, WRITE.

title: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
benchmarks: WebArena
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Rapid forgetting of potentially valuable experiences': prior web-agent methods 'discard incoming trajectories immediately after a single episode,' impeding future decision-making (S1). Navigation failures account for ~60% of web-agent errors (Fig.6) because agents operate under an 'Unknown MDP' with limited visibility into action outcomes before acting. Mitigated by the Remember paradigm: a replay-buffer directed graph G=(O,E) of visited webpages/actions transforms the task into a 'Known MDP,' and A* search (LLM-provided heuristic h(o)) over this cached graph 'substantially reduces navigation failures' (Fig.6 error analysis: R2D2 vs vanilla ReACT trajectory inspection on 60 queries). The Reflect paradigm then addresses the remaining execution failures once navigation is no longer the bottleneck, storing corrective rationale + truncated-to-error trajectory in the reflective memory.
cita: Huang et al. (2025). R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory.
notes: S3.2 Remember paradigm: replay-buffer graph (nodes=webpage observations incl. root o0, edges=(action, transition); stores DIFFS between consecutive observations, not full state) -> GRAFO; A* search (Algorithm1) with LLM-derived heuristic estimating subtree relevance selects candidate trajectories, LLM ranks final P*. S3.3 Reflect paradigm: for execution failures, LLM identifies the first erroneous action, truncates trajectory to correct prefix, generates a rationale, stores both in reflective memory. S3.4 Reflective Memory = key-value store, query encoded via dense embedding (MiniLM, retriv framework) as key (EMBEDDINGS), corrected/truncated trajectory+insight as value; TWO explicit ops: Lookup (nearest-key retrieval) and 'Update: if a newly truncated trajectory provides a more accurate or enriched reflection for an existing query, the memory updates the current value... R2D2 uses an LLM to make such decision' (ACTUALIZACION, DISCRECIONAL-LLM trigger for the update DECISION itself, layered on an EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage). Results (Table1, matches abstract): R2D2 27.3% overall SR on WebArena vs ReACT 13.1%/Tree-Search 19.0%/LATS 22.5%/AR 23.4%/BrowserGym 23.5% (best baseline); ~50% navigation-error reduction + 3x task-completion increase claimed in abstract. S4.3 ablation studies remove Remember/Reflect paradigms individually (Fig.5) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S4.4/Limitations: Table2 average-steps-per-task (ITERACION) explicit; full WebArena pass costs ~$200 GPT-4o usage (COSTO-TOKENS); step-count used as inference-latency proxy (LATENCIA). No multi-agent sharing (single ReACT-based agent) -> multiagente=NO. NEGATIVO sense(a)-adjacent: Reflect paradigm explicitly analyzes and stores insight distilled FROM failed/erroneous trajectories. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds COSTO (explicit $200/pass + step/latency accounting), PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE.

title: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution
benchmarks: SWE-Bench Verified (500 human-verified GitHub issues)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memoryless agents suffer three inefficiencies (S1): (1) redundant exploration (retry ineffective trajectories across similar issues), (2) inability of knowledge transfer (discard successful insights -- workflows, code patterns, contextual factors -- after each session), (3) lack of strategic evolution (no compounding expertise over time). Mitigated by the multi-facet Experience Bank distilled from BOTH successful AND failed trajectories: failure trajectories carry explicit failure-cause metadata (incorrect localization / flawed modification strategy / insufficient problem comprehension, S3.2) enabling targeted extraction of negative patterns alongside positive ones. RQ2 ablation (Table2, DeepSeek-V3-0324) confirms both facets independently help and combine: full SWE-Exp 42.0% vs w/o-Comprehension-Experience 38.8% vs w/o-Modification-Experience 39.4% vs w/o-Dual-Agent 39.8%.
cita: Chen et al. (2026). SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution.
notes: S3.1-3.3 four-stage OFFLINE pipeline: (1) collect repair trajectories (success+failure) from diverse repos, each tuple <directive,action,state,feedback>, annotated success/failure + failure-cause metadata; (2) Experiencer agent DISTILLS raw (lengthy/noisy/problem-specific) trajectories into 2 facets -- Comprehension Experience (perspective: how the issue was understood) + Modification Experience (generalized repair strategy) -- explicit CONSOLIDACION/abstraction step; (3) offline embedding+storage in a vector-database Experience Bank, indexed by issue_type+description (representacion=VECTOR). S3.4 online reuse: dual-agent architecture (Instructor=high-level strategy, Assistant=low-level execution) sharing retrieved experience -> multiagente=SI; before each MCTS decision node, top-N retrieved by vector similarity (EMBEDDINGS) then a RerankerAgent selects top-K (RANKING) -- integrated as contextual guidance at MCTS decision points, not a one-shot injection. Results (matches abstract): Pass@1 73.0% on SWE-Bench Verified w/ Claude 4 Sonnet, SOTA among open-source agent frameworks. Table3 Cost Analysis (S6.3): token cost 203.3K vs 189.1K baseline(SWE-Search), API cost $0.13 vs $0.12, wall time 15min49s vs 12min37s, retrieval+rerank overhead ~37.5s/instance -> COSTO-TOKENS+LATENCIA, explicit conclusion 'substantial performance gains achieved with minimal additional cost.' RQ2 ablation (Table2) isolates read-side utility of each experience facet -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): failure trajectories explicitly annotated+stored with failure-cause metadata as first-class content for targeted extraction. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, COSTO, MULTIAGENTE, PROCEDIMENTAL.
